title: Blackridge Insurance — implementation capture (on‑prem pilot)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working capture from kickoff + technical follow-up for Blackridge Insurance on-prem pilot. Meant to be a single place for call notes, constraints, immediate decisions, and next steps.

Attendees (call 2024-11-06):
- Maya Chen (Redwood, SE)
- Ravi Patel (Redwood, Solutions Eng)
- Simone Alvarez (Blackridge, Platform Architect)
- Aaron Kim (Blackridge, Security/Compliance)
- Tom Hargreaves (Blackridge, ML Lead)

High-level ask:
Blackridge wants a private deployment (air-gapped option) to power a claim-automation assistant and policy-extraction pipeline. Key constraints: no outbound internet from inference cluster, HSM-backed key material, HIPAA+state privacy controls, and predictable P95 latency under 350ms for 512-token generations at steady-state 40–60 QPS.

Environment constraints (explicit):
- Data residency: on-prem in their primary DC (East Campus).
- Network: strict egress policy — no outbound except to corporate monitoring endpoint; all Pulls must be via signed bundles pushed by ops.
- Security: KMS via their on-prem HSM (Luna 7xx). We must support customer-managed key unwrap or integrate with PKCS#11.
- Audit: 12-month immutable audit logs, SOC2+HIPAA evidence collection.
- Hardware baseline proposed by customer: 4x A100 SXM or 8x A30 (they're evaluating cost).

Performance targets and workload shape:
- Steady QPS target: 40–60 concurrent inference requests for summarization and classification flows; peak burst target 120 QPS for short windows.
- Payloads: median input tokens ~120, avg generation length ~200 tokens.
- Target: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 350ms for typical 512-token budget (mix of streaming and non-streaming).
- Priority: minimize tail latency over maximizing throughput for UX use cases.

Model and serving considerations discussed:
- Customer prefers an open model family (for licensing) — leaning toward a Llama2-style 13B variant with quantization. They asked about Redwood-verified quantized profiles and tradeoffs.
- Need to validate conversational state handling (KV cache across sessions) and secure ephemeral storage of KV (no disk writes containing PII).
- Prefers pinned model version + rollback strategy; will require canary rollout windows.
- No external fallback to Redwood hosted API allowed (due to egress rules). We proposed intra-fallback: routing to a smaller local model (7B int8) when load spikes. Need to test quality delta.

Operational points / gotchas:
- Air-gapped deploy: standard bootstrap flow (pulling images) will need an ops bundle and offline package. Our packaging team must produce a signed offline artifact and instructions for chassis/node preparation.
- HSM integration is not yet validated — PKCS#11 shim in our private control plane has partial support. Action: run HSM integration lab with their Luna device model.
- Metrics & observability: they require token-level cost attribution per tenant/team. On-prem console must expose token counts and per-route latency breakdown.
- Logging: audit logs must never contain raw PII. We need to ensure redaction rules for stack traces and request payloads are strict by default.
- PR compliance: legal wants export-control checklist for models (public/open vs restricted). Onus on us to provide model provenance docs.

Immediate action items (owners + rough ETA):
1) Offline package for East Campus (artifact + install runbook) — Owner: Ravi Patel — ETA: 2024-11-20
2) HSM integration test: lab run with Luna emulator and Luna 7xx spec — Owner: Aaron Kim (coordinate w/ infra) — ETA: 2024-11-15
3) Latency/throughput simulation: create a synthetic perf profile using customer token distributions (120/200 tokens) and evaluate 13B quantized vs 7B int8 on their candidate hardware (4x A100 vs 8x A30) — Owner: Tom Hargreaves + Redwood perf eng (Simone to share hardware config) — ETA: 2024-11-18
4) Audit & redaction rules doc: sketch for legal/security review — Owner: Maya Chen — ETA: 2024-11-12
5) Canary/fallback plan doc (no-hosted-fallback): define criteria and safe rollback — Owner: Ravi Patel — ETA: 2024-11-14
6) Compliance packet: model provenance + SOC2/HIPAA mapping checklist — Owner: Aaron Kim — ETA: 2024-11-19

Questions we need from Blackridge (Simone / Aaron to confirm):
- Will ops allow a single outbound TCP egress to a signed artifact repository during install? If not, what is the approved bundle transfer mechanism (USB, secure SCP from their bastion)?
- Confirm required retention window and encryption at rest standard (AES-256, FIPS?).
- Exact traffic shaping expectations during business hours vs batch windows (affects autoscaling aggressiveness).

Notes from the call (raw):
- Simone: "No external dependencies during runtime — we need full operations hands-off after install."
- Aaron: "HSM is non-negotiable for key material. We cannot put key unwrap on any cloud KMS."
- Tom: "We can accept slightly higher P50 if tail is predictable; UX team will triage anything >500ms."

Testing plan (draft):
- Phase A (lab): perf bench on our infra using replicated token shape, verify model latency with and without KV cache warm-up; quantify quality delta between 13B quantized and 7B fallback.
- Phase B (on-prem dry run): offline install by Blackridge ops with Redwood remote observer, run synthetic traffic to validate autoscaling and canary.
- Phase C (pilot): limited internal rollout to claims team (5% of traffic), collect quality metrics and rollback criteria for 2 weeks.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: HSM mismatch causes delay — Mitigation: spin up early shim dev + schedule vendor co-ordinate call.
- Risk: Air-gap install errors — Mitigation: provide runbook + pre-flight checklist and an on-site option (paid).
- Risk: Model quality at 7B fallback unacceptable — Mitigation: tune prompts, use reranking cached results, or increase capacity for 13B.

Reference links and artifacts: see linked_artifacts above. More helpful: internal perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness (private).

Open decisions to surface in next sync (2024-11-13 planning):
- Finalize hardware footprint (A100 vs A30) — cost vs latency tradeoff.
- Agree on egress/install mechanism.
- Confirm whether Blackridge legal needs additional model provenance artifacts beyond our standard packet.

Next sync: 2024-11-13 11:00 PT (tentative) — plan to cover status of action items and HSM lab results.

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal and mirror to Confluence once HSM path validated. Use ticket BR-3421 for tracking all infra tasks.

-- End capture (Maya, 2024-11-06)
